svg.title: The security toolkit shared by NTAG213, NTAG215 and NTAG216 — and its shared ceiling
svg.desc: A teal shield with a check mark is labelled identical on NTAG213, 215 and 216: security is never the tiebreaker. Beside it, three feature cards list the shared toolkit: a 32-bit password with 16-bit PACK that locks a page range against reads or writes; the ECDSA originality signature, read via the READ_SIG command and verified against NXP's published public key to prove genuine silicon; and the optional NFC read counter, useful for tap analytics but not a cryptographic proof. A fourth, red-tinted card states the shared ceiling: no AES, no CMAC, no per-tap SUN URLs — applications that need a fresh cryptographic URL on every tap require NTAG 424 DNA, a different chip rather than a bigger 21x.
svg.text: SECURITY — SPOILER: IT IS A TIE
One toolkit on all three chips, and one shared ceiling
locks a page range against reads or writes — stops tags being rewritten after deployment
factory-programmed proof of genuine NXP silicon — verify against NXP's published public key
counts taps for analytics and crude anomaly checks — a number, not a cryptographic proof
The shared ceiling: no AES, no CMAC, no per-tap SUN URLs
need a fresh cryptographic URL on every tap to beat motivated counterfeiters?
that is NTAG 424 DNA territory — a different chip, not a bigger 21x
Pick the chip by memory; pick the family by threat model.
